steps.text: Mix sugar, butter, milk, cocoa, and salt together in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Boil for 1 minute.
Stir in oats, peanut butter, and vanilla. Drop by tablespoonfuls onto waxed paper. Allow to cool and harden, 30 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Preacher Cookies
raw_recipe.description: No oven's needed for this no-bake cookie recipe that turns chewy oats, crunchy peanut butter, and a boiled chocolate mixture into yummy treats!
raw_recipe.name: Preacher Cookies

recipeInstructions.text: Mix sugar, butter, milk, cocoa, and salt together in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Boil for 1 minute.
Stir in oats, peanut butter, and vanilla. Drop by tablespoonfuls onto waxed paper. Allow to cool and harden, 30 to 45 minutes.

review.reviewBody: These came out great, and my boys love em' too! I only had a half stick of butter on hand, so I used 1/4 cup shortening as well. For those that were finding they were to runny, make sure you boil the full minute, and then after all ingredients are mixed in, I stirred them in the pot for a little while to help the "dough" cool and harden a bit, as they were runny until they cooled a little in the pot. Then drop them on your wax paper, they should form great at that point.

I've been making these cookies since I was a little girl (we always called them 3 minute or No Bake cookies). I also use creamy peanut butter and I sometimes immediately pour the mixture into a 13x9 pan (lightly greased) to make bar cookies, instead of the drop cookies.

I use this recipe as a base. Like Becky I found they didn’t stay together. I add extras such as chopped nuts and those left over cereal crumbs. Instead of cookies I press the mixture in a 9x12 pan lined with parchment, cool in fridge, then cut into squares. Fast and easy.

These were my favorite as a child;when I would visit my Granny my favorite Aunt that took care of my Granny would make them. I prefer them with oats but she always used graham crackers(14 whole graham crackers broken into pieces for any that want to know) and they were a fantastic treat for a poor girl that didn't get treats often, especially homemade. Easy to make and using a candy thermometer (235°) is the best because if they're overcooked they get dry and undercooked they won't set properly, just like fudge. Well, it's fudge with add-ins, right? Love it.

Perfect little no-bake chocolate-peanut butter cookie. Personally, I always use butter because I think it tastes better than margarine and, margarine has more water in it and can, sometimes, make the cookie a little soggy. Also, the key to making sure that these cookies set up or harden the way you want them to is to make sure that the sugar has dissolved completely while boiling. Be sure that the mixture has come to a full boil, where it is really bubbling well, stirring constantly so as not to burn the ingredients. Once the mixture has come to a full boil, be sure to boil (and stir) for a full minute, or even a little longer. I like to boil the mixture for about a minute and a half to two minutes to make sure the sugar has completely dissolved. Just be sure to stir the sugar mixture constantly and watch it closely so as not to burn and you should never have a problem with soggy cookies again. If you've ever made candy before, you know that your sugar has to come to a certain temperature before it will set up correctly. These cookies are similar in that you really want your sugar to come to a full boil and boil for at least a full minute or you end up with what I call spoon cookies because you'll have to eat them with a spoon. ;)

I love this recipe, i made these cookies all during high school. For those of you who have said the cookies are too runny or don’t harden correctly: i always boiled the mixture for three minutes. I like mine extra crumbly though. Try boiling for two and see if that works.

Been making these for over 50 years. We call them Hamburger Cookies. I guess because the texture looks like hamburger. Our recipe increases pnut butter to 1 cup and 2 tsp of vanilla. We cook 2 min of a full rolling boil. This is my family's favorite cookie.

These cookies were delicious, however, they were super sweet! Almost sickeningly so. Half of a cookie each and my husband and I were on a sugar high. Next time I will probably use 1/2 a cup less sugar and definitely add more peanut butter. Also, I let them harden in the refrigerator and they were set in less than 10 minutes. Thank you for the quick, easy and ultimately delicious recipe!

Absolutely amazing. We have a recipe for chocolate oatmeal no bake cookies but I picked this one up because freezing isn’t necessary. I do prefer them cold but back when we had a tiny freezer this was helpful. I saw several reviews saying that they didn’t harden or got crumbly but I have the solution. You need to make sure you boil for EXACTLY one minuet, these cookies can be picky. Too short and they’re watery, too long and they’re dry and crumbly. Family loves these and they’re great for a hot day or a sudden chocolate emergency.
I love this recipe and have made it many times. For a Mexican chocolate version, add 2 tbsp chili powder and 1/2 tsp cinnamon. It adds a tiny spicy tingle at the end. My coworkers loved it.

Very good. Make sure that the boil is full before starting your 1 minute timer. Make sure the bubbles are in full roll all the way to the edge of the saucepan. Then start. I usually boil at 7-8 of 10 on the heater dial. It sometimes takes over a minute for the boil to evenly cover the saucepan.
These were so easy! Still waiting for them to harden but I think they will be fine. I remember them from school & they were called Cow Patties.

I'm 67 and these look exactly like what we always knew as "Yummies" (That's what my Nan's recipe called them, although I don't know where she got the recipe from) The only difference I can see between Yummies and Preacher Cookies is that Yummies don't have peanut butter in, but does have some desiccated coconut. So simple. Boil, mix, drop in rough spoonfuls (no shaping required), cool and eat. We used to love scraping the saucepan after.
Made for the first time. Mom and I loved it!
This was the first cookie I ever made by myself, around age 10. Close to 50 years later, they are still a family favorite!
I see lots of names for these. A friend calls them "S______ Bears." Lol. Whatever you call them, they're great.
No need to change perfect.if it ain't broken don't fix it !
